Question Choices: Select all that apply. Statistics involves: Collecting-data Presenting-data Analyzing-data
Hints: Think about what we do with information.
Solution: Statistics is about working with data: collecting it, organizing/presenting it, and analyzing it.

Question Choices: Is this statistical? "Do you like soccer?" Answer yes or no
Solution: Only one answer -> no data variability -> not statistical

Question Choices: Which is statistical? A. "What is tomorrow's bus fare?"  B. "How much do students spend on lunch each day this month?"
Hints: Think about the number of data points
Solution: A -> one value -> not statistical. B -> many values -> variability -> statistical

Question Choices: Two classes recorded reading time (in hours): Class A: 2, 2.1, 2, 2.2, 2.1  Class B: 1, 3.5, 2, 4, 0.5. Which class has more variability? Answer A or B
Solution: Class A -> little change. Class B -> numbers vary a lot -> higher variability

Question Choices: Select. Change this question to a statistical question. "How many minutes did I exercise today?": How-many-minutes-did-I-exercise-today-and-yesterday? How-many-minutes-do-students-in-my-class-exercise-each-day? Did-I-exercise-today?
Hints: A statistical question needs many data points with variability.
Solution: Only the class-wide question includes many students whose answers vary -> statistical
